correctness.rationale: A flex gives O_E(1)=3O. Abel and the restriction isomorphism H0(P2,O(2))≅H0(E,O_E(2)) give a bijection between six-distinct-point conics and zero-sum six-subsets of T; Bezout excludes extra contacts. Character orthogonality produces 1,928,772 using exact coefficients 156,238,908, -1,101, 6 with 1, 8, 72 characters. A three-point group count gives 720 trisecants with 30 through each point. Pair counting gives exactly 227,520 reducible conics via 632 disjoint triples per line; smoothness is the complement. The GL2(Z/9) action ensures uniform incidence counts. The independent standard-library verifier agrees by dynamic programming and exhaustive disjoint-pair enumeration.

evidence: The 2022 six-secant calculation uses 27 points E[6] minus E[3], gives 8,244 total and 5,976 smooth, and proposes studying curves through higher-order division points.
The 2024 paper determines 72 type-nine points and counts 324 3+3 bitangent conics.

The 2026 thesis exhibits three special 24-line subarrangements through these type-nine points and studies the same 3+3-contact conics; no full 720-line/six-distinct-point census appears in the inspected material.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2022 count is for a distinct level structure; neither its theorem nor the 2024/2026 tangency results dominates the six-transverse-point count. The 2026 special pencils exhibit 72 lines but do not cover all zero-sum triples.

evidence: Gattazzo’s type-nine collinearity lemma predicts possible third intersections but does not count the number of lines through each point or disjoint pairs of lines.
The 2022 count for sextactic points cannot be substituted directly: its group is (Z/6Z)^2 with a 27-point complement, while the present group is (Z/9Z)^2 with 72 points.
A 3P+3Q divisor has only two support points and hence is disjoint from the specified six-point transverse-contact class.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The candidate does not simply restate or take a special case of the inspected prior results; it resolves an adjacent enumerative gap by a separate order-nine character count and complete reducible-line decomposition.

evidence: Six distinct type-nine points have a unique conic if and only if they sum to zero; this makes the proposed theorem an exact zero-sum six-subset count in (Z/9Z)^2 excluding its 3-torsion subgroup.
The 1979 treatment proves the third point on a line through two type-nine points is again type nine or a flex; it does not give the zero-sum six-subset census.
The 2024 type-nine conics have intersection divisor 3P+3Q with P and Q distinct, whereas a conic in this finding has divisor P1+...+P6 with all six points distinct.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Comparison of divisors and exact torsion subsets rules out equivalence to the published 3+3-contact count. General Abel conditions alone do not imply the new explicit character, reducible, and incidence counts without further enumeration.

evidence: Inspected numerical tables and stated totals in the related original papers include 8,244/5,976, 324, 72, and the 24-line pencils; they do not list 1,928,772/227,520/1,701,252, 720, or the new per-point incidences.
Exact-number literature discovery for 1,928,772, 1,701,252 and 227,520 in conjunction with elliptic conics did not surface an equivalent research statement.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No exact table of this six-point type-nine configuration was identified. Absence from a sampled search index is a residual-risk assessment, not a uniqueness or priority proof.

originality.rationale: The exact 1,928,772/227,520/1,701,252 six-distinct-type-nine-point conic census, complete 720-trisecant configuration, and per-point incidences are not stated or logically forced by the inspected primary sources. The 1979 source develops type-nine points and collinearity closure, the 2022 source counts six-secant conics for a different 27-point torsion locus, and the 2024 source and 2026 thesis count conics with 3+3 tangency, not six transverse contacts. Novelty remains provisional against unindexed sources.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier conic count for 9-division points, or an independently derived general torsion-subset formula, could imply the displayed numbers even if no matching title or exact table is discoverable.
The reviewed scope is geometric counts of reduced plane conics; scheme-theoretic deformation multiplicities and mutual conic intersections are not claimed.

value.rationale: The 2022 sextactic-six-secant problem explicitly motivates moving to higher-order division points, and the 2024 study identifies the natural 72 type-nine points without their six-secant census. This theorem completes the precise full six-point conic and reducible-subarrangement counts at that next intrinsic torsion level, for every smooth complex plane cubic. The 720-line incidence structure and exact per-point numbers are useful natural invariants of the point configuration; value does not depend on hypothetical downstream claims.
